Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the recap and the one-pager — useful. A couple clarifying points from our side to help you scope the deep-dive: 

- Data classification: most of the data is PHI-adjacent (patient identifiers + notes). We need to ensure that logs and any persisted model artifacts cannot be cross-tenant accessible.
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) with the ability to rotate keys and have key access logs forwarded to our SIEM.
- Control plane: question — does Redwood's control plane see unencrypted payloads or only metadata? We need explicit guarantees for encryption-in-flight and at-rest, and whether anything is stored in SaaS control plane.

As for deployment mode, we are evaluating:
A) Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity in Redwood’s environment but with strict network isolation and encryption controls.
B) Private VPC (hosted): Redwood’s control plane is in our VPC or a customer-controlled control plane, or fully on-prem if required.

Prefer to have David and Dev on the deep-dive. Our procurement lead (Matt) copied for timeline.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & data isolation — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Tom — thanks, quick technical clarifications below before the call: 

- Control plane data: by default our hosted control plane handles orchestration and metadata; customer payloads are never stored in plaintext in the control plane. For Hosted and Dedicated we support TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. For Dedicated we can limit telemetry and provide stricter retention windows.
- Customer-managed KMS: supported for Private VPC and Private/on-prem deployments (full BYOK). For Dedicated (Redwood-hosted reserved capacity) we offer a customer-key option where keys are provisioned into an HSM we manage but with restricted access and logging — not full BYOK in every case. We can discuss bringing an HSM into customer VPC for private deployments.
- Network isolation: Dedicated includes isolated GPU pools; Private VPC gives you a customer network boundary and optional air-gapped on-prem.

We'll layout concrete configurations in the deep-dive doc — I'll prep a network diagram and a table of what is supported today vs roadmap.

-David

Hi all — thanks for the quick replies. A few practical notes to help procurement and security triage: 

- If your security policy requires absolute customer-managed keys and no HSM we control, Private VPC or on-prem is the cleanest path. That gives you full control over KMS and network ingress/egress.
- If you'd prefer faster time-to-production with most isolation guarantees and are amenable to our customer-key-in-managed-HSM model, Dedicated (reserved capacity) typically hits your latency/cost targets while keeping data isolated at the tenant level. For many healthcare customers we start with Dedicated and then migrate to Private for regulated workloads that need stricter key ownership.
- Control plane observability: for Private deployments we can push detailed audit logs and telemetry into your log collector (Splunk/Datadog) and disable non-critical telemetry.
- Suggested artifacts for the security deep-dive: network diagram (we'll provide), key management flow, retention policy table, SOC2 attestations, penetration test summary. I've attached the one-pager and a draft MAP.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue Mar 17, 10:00-11:30am PT or Wed Mar 18, 2:00-3:30pm PT. Which works?
